51450179.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant N-terminal FLAG/His6-tagged human vanin-1 expressed in CHO cells assessed as dissociation constant by surface plasmon resonance analysis
51450179.original_paragraph: Experiments were conducted using a BIACORE T200 (GE Healthcare) using CM5 sensor chips.  Neutravidin (Pierce) was added to the CM5 channels using amine  coupling (GE Healthcare) (pH 5 at 25°C) to an average density of  25,000 resonance units (RUs). Biotinylated vanin1 was next immobilized (75 μg/mL at 5 μL/min) in a buﬀer (20 mM HEPES  pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl) to a final density of 1000−8000 RU depending on the aﬃnity of the compound tested. No protein was added to channel 1. Compounds were prepared from neat DMSO solutions; each compound was tested over 12 concentration points (twofold dilutions) centered on the compound IC50. The final assay buﬀer was  20 mM HEPES, pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, and 0.5% DMSO. Experiments were conducted at 25°C with a flow rate of 60 μL/min; injection and  dissociation times were between 30−60 and 90−300 s depending on the aﬃnity of the compound tested. Compound-dependent responses  were subtracted from channel 1 and a zero-concentration buﬀer blank  prior to analysis. Dissociation equilibrium constants (KD), association constants (kon), and dissociation constants (koff) were determined using  a binary association model within the software (T200 BIA Eval)  supplied by the manufacturer and are reported in Table 4.
